headline: Australia's S&P/ASX 200 Falls for Sixth Session as Mining Stocks Slump
summary: Australia's benchmark S&P/ASX 200 index fell 0.9% to 8,821.80, extending its losing streak to six days. Mining shares dropped 3.5% following a decline in global copper prices.
why: The Australian equity market is heavily weighted toward resource extraction companies, making its benchmark index sensitive to industrial metal prices.

impacts.name: S&P/ASX 200
impacts.why: Falling copper prices and weak employment figures dragged down major mining constituents.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: Broad weakness across industrial metals hurt major resource constituents, pulling down the index.
